{{Quote|Thank you for selecting our brand of mini-transmitter. If you assemble it properly, following the instructions I am about to give you, it will provide many years of fun, and valuable service to you.|Dromboid, hosting an instruction cassette|<ref name="SWHS">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref>}}
A '''company''' sold [[mini-transmitter]]s&mdash;devices that could translate speech into one of 1,000 other [[Language/Legends|languages]]&mdash;during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Although the company manufactured its products in the [[Amorphiia system/Legends|Amorphiia system]],<ref name="SWHS" /> by [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="date">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=870#15778940|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2006-10-12|time=6:13 PM}}</ref> the items were available in other regions of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. That year, the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Lumpawaroo/Legends|Lumpawarrump]] constructed one of this company's mini-transmitters on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]].<ref name="SWHS" />

Each mini-transmitter shipped with a bag of tools, a [[circuit-breaker module]], an [[impulse-to-voice translator]], and an [[instruction cassette]] to explain the assembly process.<ref name="SWHS" /> This cassette was hosted by a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Amorphiian]] named [[Dromboid]].<ref name="Dromboid">The article {{InsiderCite|106|I Have a Bad Feeling About This!}} uses the name "Dromboid" in conjunction with this character, but it does no specify whether it is the character's proper name or an alternative name for his species. However, the 4th draft script for ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'' p. 109A, confirms that the character's name is in fact Dromboid.</ref> Despite his best efforts, Dromboid's tendency to speed up and slow down erratically, common to his [[Species/Legends|species]], proved frustrating to Lumpwarrump. Nevertheless, the announcement preceding the instructional cassette insisted that the host's malfunctions did not affect the product itself.<ref name="SWHS" />

==Behind the scenes==
The mini-transmitter company is mentioned in ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'', a television variety show that aired on [[CBS]] in [[1978]]. In the special, the Wookiee Lumpawarrump, played by [[Patty Maloney]], follows the instructions of Dromboid, played by [[Harvey Korman]], to assemble one of the company's devices.
